title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Civil Affairs on Issuing the Opinions on Several Issues Concerning Lawfully Handling Acts of Guardians Infringing upon Minors' Rights and Interests
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Civil Affairs

Notice on Issuing the Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Lawful Handling of Acts of Guardians Infringing upon the Rights and Interests of Minors

Fa Fa [2014] No. 24

The High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Public Security Departments (Bureaus), and Civil Affairs Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, the Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army, and the Security Department of the General Political Department; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, the People's Procuratorate of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, the Public Security Bureau, and the Civil Affairs Bureau:

The Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Lawful Handling of Acts of Guardians Infringing upon the Rights and Interests of Minors are hereby issued to you for implementation from January 1, 2015. Please strictly comply with and enforce them. Any issues arising during implementation and the circumstances encountered shall be promptly reported to the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Civil Affairs respectively.

December 18, 2014

Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Lawful Handling of Acts of Guardians Infringing upon the Rights and Interests of Minors

To effectively safeguard the lawful rights and interests of minors, strengthen the administrative protection and judicial protection of minors, and ensure that minors receive proper guardianship and care, these Opinions are formulated in accordance with the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law on the Protection of Minors of the People's Republic of China, and other legal provisions, concerning the relevant work on handling acts of guardians infringing upon the rights and interests of minors (hereinafter referred to as "guardianship infringement acts").

I. General Provisions

1. For the purposes of these Opinions, "guardianship infringement acts" refer to acts by parents or other guardians (hereinafter referred to as "guardians") including sexual assault, sale, abandonment, abuse, violent injury of minors; instigating or using minors to commit illegal or criminal acts; coercing, luring, or using minors to beg; and failing to perform guardianship duties, thereby seriously endangering the physical and mental health of minors.

2. The handling of guardianship infringement acts shall adhere to the principle of the best interests of the minor, fully consider the minor's physical and mental characteristics and personal dignity, and provide special and priority protection to the minor.

3. Any organization or individual has the right to dissuade, stop, or report guardianship infringement acts.

Public security organs shall take measures to promptly stop guardianship infringement acts discovered in the course of work or reported by units and individuals, and in emergency situations, remove the minor from the guardian.

Civil affairs departments shall establish minor rescue and protection institutions (including rescue management stations and minor rescue and protection centers) to assume temporary guardianship responsibilities for minors who enter such institutions due to guardianship infringement, and when necessary, apply to the people's court for the revocation of the guardian's qualification.

People's courts shall lawfully accept applications for personal safety protection rulings and cases for the revocation of guardian qualifications, and render judgments.

People's procuratorates shall lawfully exercise legal supervision over the work of public security organs and people's courts in handling guardianship infringement acts.

Where people's courts, people's procuratorates, or public security organs have specialized working bodies for handling cases involving minors, such specialized working bodies shall give priority to handling guardianship infringement cases.

4. People's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, and civil affairs departments shall fully perform their duties, strengthen guidance and training, and improve their capacity and capability to protect minors; strengthen communication and cooperation, establish an information sharing mechanism, and achieve effective integration of administrative protection and judicial protection for minors.

5. People's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, and civil affairs departments shall strengthen coordination and cooperation with the Working Committee on Women and Children, education departments, health departments, the Communist Youth League, the Women's Federation, the Committee for the Care of the Next Generation, the village (neighborhood) committee of the minor's place of residence, etc., and actively guide, encourage, and support legal service institutions, social work service institutions, public welfare charitable organizations, and volunteers and other social forces to jointly carry out the protection of minors subject to guardianship infringement.

II. Reporting and Handling

6. Schools, hospitals, village (neighborhood) committees, social work service institutions, and their staff members shall promptly report or file a complaint with the public security organ when discovering that a minor is subject to guardianship infringement.

Other units, their staff members, and individuals shall also promptly report or file a complaint with the public security organ when discovering that a minor is subject to guardianship infringement.

7. After receiving a report or complaint concerning a guardianship infringement act, the public security organ shall immediately dispatch police to handle the matter, stop the ongoing infringement act, and promptly conduct an investigation. Where the circumstances meet the conditions for criminal case filing, a criminal case shall be immediately docketed and investigated.

8. When handling guardianship infringement cases, public security organs shall, in accordance with statutory procedures, collect and fix evidence promptly and comprehensively to ensure the quality of case handling.

When questioning a minor, consideration shall be given to the minor's physical and mental characteristics, and a gentle manner shall be adopted to prevent further harm.

If the minor has another guardian, that other guardian shall be notified to be present. If the other guardian cannot be notified or fails to appear, other adult relatives of the minor, representatives from the minor's school, the village (neighborhood) committee, a minor protection organization, and professional social workers may be notified to be present.

9. If the guardian's guardianship infringement act constitutes an act violating public security administration, the public security organ shall lawfully impose a public security administrative penalty; but if the circumstances are extremely minor and no public security administrative penalty is imposed, the guardian shall be given criticism and education, and the matter shall be reported to the local village (neighborhood) committee. If the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued according to law.

10. For a guardian suspected of suffering from mental disorder who has already committed acts endangering the minor's safety or poses a risk of endangering the minor's safety, the guardian's close relatives, the guardian's work unit, and the local public security organ shall immediately take measures to stop such acts and send the guardian to a medical institution for diagnosis of mental disorder.

11. During police dispatch, if a public security organ finds that a minor has suffered serious physical injury, faces a serious threat to personal safety, or is in a dangerous state such as being unattended, the public security organ shall remove the minor from the guardian committing the guardianship infringement act and transport the minor to the nearest other guardian, relative, village (neighborhood) committee, or minor rescue and protection institution, and complete a written handover procedure. If the minor has the ability to express opinions, the minor's opinion regarding the place of transport shall be sought.

The unit or person responsible for receiving the minor (hereinafter referred to as "temporary caregiver") shall provide temporary emergency shelter and short-term living care for the minor, protect the minor's personal safety, and shall not infringe upon the minor's lawful rights and interests.

The public security organ shall inform the temporary caregiver in writing that the temporary caregiver has the right to apply to the people's court for a personal safety protection ruling and for the revocation of the guardian's qualification according to law.

12. For a minor who has suffered serious physical injury and requires medical treatment, the public security organ shall first send the minor for medical treatment and at the same time notify another relative with guardianship qualifications to provide care, or notify the local minor rescue and protection institution to carry out follow-up relief work.

The guardian shall bear the medical treatment expenses according to law. Other relatives or the minor rescue and protection institution and others who advance the medical treatment expenses have the right to recover such expenses from the guardian.

13. When a public security organ transports a minor subject to guardianship infringement to a minor rescue and protection institution, the public security organ shall, within five working days, provide a description of the case investigation and handling status.

14. If a guardianship infringement act may constitute the crime of abuse, the public security organ shall inform the minor and the minor's close relatives of their right to file a private prosecution or to have a private prosecution filed on their behalf, and report the matter to the people's procuratorate at the same level in the same locality.

If the minor and the minor's close relatives do not file a private prosecution, the people's procuratorate shall initiate a public prosecution.

III. Temporary Placement and Personal Safety Protection Rulings

15. The minor rescue and protection institution shall accept minors subject to guardianship infringement who are transported by the public security organ, and perform temporary guardianship responsibilities.

The period of temporary guardianship performed by the minor rescue and protection institution shall generally not exceed one year.

16. The minor rescue and protection institution may adopt methods such as foster care, voluntary assistance, institutional care, or placement in a designated boarding school designated by the government to provide temporary care for the minor, and provide services such as psychological counseling and emotional comfort for the minor.

If the minor needs to transfer schools or enroll in a different locality for compulsory education due to temporary guardianship, the education administrative department shall provide guarantees.

17. If another guardian or close relative of the minor requests to care for the minor, after the public security organ or the village (neighborhood) committee confirms the identity of that person, the minor rescue and protection institution may hand over the minor to that person for care and terminate the temporary guardianship.

If other close relatives or friends request to care for the minor, with the consent of the minor's father's or mother's work unit or the village (neighborhood) committee, the minor rescue and protection institution may hand over the minor to that person for care and terminate the temporary guardianship.

When the minor rescue and protection institution hands over the minor to relatives or friends for temporary care, a written handover procedure shall be completed, and the temporary caregiver shall be notified in writing of the right to apply to the people's court for a personal safety protection ruling and for the revocation of the guardian's qualification according to law.

18. The minor rescue and protection institution may organize social work service institutions and other social forces to carry out educational guidance work such as guardianship guidance and psychological counseling for the guardian, and conduct investigation and assessment of the minor's basic family situation, guardianship situation, the guardian's repentance, the minor's physical and mental health status, and the minor's wishes. The guardian's acceptance of educational guidance and subsequent performance shall be an important part of the investigation and assessment report.

Relevant units and individuals shall cooperate in carrying out the investigation and assessment work.

19. The minor rescue and protection institution shall hold consultations with the public security organ, the village (neighborhood) committee, the school, and the minor's relatives, based on the description of the case investigation and handling status, the investigation and assessment report, and the guardian's acceptance of educational guidance, and after soliciting the opinions of the minor who has the ability to express themselves, form a consultation conclusion.

If, through consultation, it is determined that the dangerous state specified in Article 11, Paragraph 1 of these Opinions has been eliminated and the guardian is able to properly perform guardianship duties, the minor rescue and protection institution shall promptly notify the guardian to retrieve the minor. The guardian shall retrieve the minor within three days and complete a written handover procedure. Before the consultation conclusion is formed, the minor rescue and protection institution shall not allow the guardian to retrieve the minor.

If, through consultation, it is determined that the guardianship infringement act falls under the circumstances specified in Article 35 of these Opinions, the minor rescue and protection institution shall apply to the people's court for the revocation of the guardian's qualification.

20. When the minor rescue and protection institution notifies the guardian to retrieve the minor, it shall report the relevant circumstances to the minor's school, the local police station, and the village (neighborhood) committee, and inform them of their duty of confidentiality regarding the content of the notification.

21. After the guardian retrieves the minor, the minor rescue and protection institution shall guide the village (neighborhood) committee to conduct follow-up visits on the guardian's guardianship and carry out educational guidance work.

The minor rescue and protection institution may also organize social work service institutions and other social forces to carry out the work specified in the preceding paragraph.

22. The minor rescue and protection institution or other temporary caregiver may, as needed, apply to the people's court of the minor's place of residence, the guardian's place of residence, or the place where the infringement occurred for a personal safety protection ruling before litigation.

The minor rescue and protection institution or other temporary caregiver may also apply to the people's court for a personal safety protection ruling during litigation.

23. After accepting an application for a personal safety protection ruling, the people's court shall issue a ruling in accordance with Articles 100, 101, and 102 of the Civil Procedure Law. If, after review, it is determined that there is a risk of infringement on the minor's personal safety, a personal safety protection ruling shall be issued.

After accepting an application for a personal safety protection ruling made before litigation, the people's court shall issue a ruling within 48 hours. If an application for a personal safety protection ruling is accepted during litigation and the circumstances are urgent, a ruling shall also be issued within 48 hours. The personal safety protection ruling shall be enforced immediately.

24. A personal safety protection ruling may include one or more of the following contents:

(1) Prohibiting the respondent from violently injuring or threatening the minor or the minor's temporary caregiver;

(2) Prohibiting the respondent from following, harassing, or contacting the minor or the minor's temporary caregiver;

(3) Ordering the respondent to move out of the minor's residence;

(4) Other measures to protect the personal safety of the minor and the minor's temporary caregiver.

25. If the respondent refuses to comply with the personal safety protection ruling, endangering the personal safety of the minor or the minor's temporary caregiver or disrupting the work order of the minor rescue and protection institution, the minor, the minor rescue and protection institution, or other temporary caregiver has the right to report to the public security organ, and the public security organ shall handle the matter according to law.

If the respondent commits other acts of refusing to comply with the personal safety protection ruling, the minor, the minor rescue and protection institution, or other temporary caregiver has the right to report to the people's court, and the people's court shall, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, impose a fine or detention in accordance with Articles 111, 115, and 116 of the Civil Procedure Law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued according to law.

26. If a party is dissatisfied with a personal safety protection ruling, the party may apply for reconsideration once. The enforcement of the ruling shall not be suspended during the reconsideration period.

IV. Litigation for Application for Revocation of Guardian Qualification

27. The following units and persons (hereinafter referred to as "relevant units and persons") have the right to apply to the people's court for the revocation of the guardian's qualification:

(1) Other guardians of the minor, paternal grandparents, maternal grandparents, elder brothers, elder sisters, and other close relatives and friends having a close relationship;

(2) The village (neighborhood) committee of the minor's place of residence, the work unit of the minor's father or mother;

(3) The civil affairs department and the minor rescue and protection institution established by it;

(4) Organizations and units such as the Communist Youth League, the Women's Federation, the Committee for the Care of the Next Generation, and schools.

An application for revocation of the guardian's qualification shall generally be filed by the unit or person responsible for the temporary care of the minor as specified in the preceding paragraph, and may also be filed by other units and persons as specified in the preceding paragraph.

28. When applying to the people's court for revocation of the guardian's qualification, the relevant unit or person shall submit relevant evidence.

If there is an investigation and assessment report containing information on the minor's basic situation, guardianship problems, the guardian's repentance, the guardian's acceptance of educational guidance, the minor's physical and mental health status, and the minor's wishes, such report shall also be submitted together.

29. If a relevant unit or person requests the public security organ or the people's procuratorate to issue relevant case evidence materials, the public security organ or the people's procuratorate shall provide basic materials or written explanations proving the facts of the case.

30. In cases where a guardian is prosecuted for a guardianship infringement act, the people's procuratorate shall notify the minor and the minor's temporary caregiver in writing of their right to apply for revocation of the guardian's qualification according to law.

If the guardianship infringement act meets the circumstances specified in Article 35 of these Opinions but the relevant unit or person has not filed a lawsuit, the people's procuratorate shall issue a written suggestion to the local civil affairs department or minor rescue and protection institution to apply to the people's court for revocation of the guardian's qualification.

31. Cases for revocation of guardian qualification shall be under the jurisdiction of the basic people's court of the minor's place of residence, the guardian's place of residence, or the place where the infringement occurred.

No litigation fees shall be charged for accepting a case for revocation of guardian qualification.

V. Trial of Cases for Revocation of Guardian Qualification and Post-Judgment Placement

32. The people's court shall try cases for revocation of guardian qualification in accordance with the special procedure provided for in the Civil Procedure Law, and conclude the case within one month. If there are special circumstances requiring an extension, the extension shall be approved by the president of the court.

33. The people's court shall comprehensively review the investigation and assessment report and other evidence materials, and hear the opinions of the respondent, the minor who has the ability to express opinions, and the village (neighborhood) committee, the school, neighbors, etc.

34. The people's court may, as needed, engage appropriate persons from the community to conduct social observation and protection of the minor, and may introduce a psychological counseling and assessment mechanism, organizing professional social workers, child psychology experts, and other professionals to participate in the litigation, providing psychological counseling and assessment services to the minor and the respondent.

35. If the respondent has any of the following circumstances, the people's court may render a judgment revoking the respondent's guardian qualification:

(1) Sexual assault, sale, abandonment, abuse, or violent injury of a minor, seriously harming the minor's physical and mental health;

(2) Placing the minor in a state without supervision and care, causing the minor to face danger of death or serious injury, and failing to change after education;

(3) Refusing to perform guardianship duties for six months or more, causing the minor to become homeless or without means of subsistence;

(4) Having bad habits such as drug use, gambling, or long-term heavy drinking, making it impossible to properly perform guardianship duties, or being unable to perform guardianship duties due to imprisonment or other reasons, and refusing to delegate part or all of the guardianship duties to others, causing the minor to be in a difficult or dangerous situation;

(5) Coercing, luring, or using the minor to beg, and after three or more criticisms and education by the public security organ, the minor rescue and protection institution, or other departments, still refusing to correct, seriously affecting the minor's normal life and study;

(6) Instigating or using the minor to commit illegal or criminal acts, with egregious circumstances;

(7) Other acts seriously infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of the minor.

36. If a judgment revokes the guardian's qualification and the minor has another guardian, that other guardian shall assume guardianship duties. The other guardian shall take measures to prevent the minor from continuing to suffer infringement.

If there is no other guardian, the people's court shall, in accordance with the principle of the best interests of the minor, designate a guardian from among the persons and units specified in Article 16, Paragraphs 2 and 4 of the General Principles of the Civil Law. When designating an individual as guardian, consideration shall be given to the individual's willingness, conduct, physical condition, economic conditions, emotional connection with the minor's life, and the wishes of the minor who has the ability to express opinions.

If there is no suitable person or other unit to serve as guardian, the people's court shall designate the civil affairs department as guardian, and the civil affairs department's affiliated child welfare institution shall accept and raise the minor.

37. If the judgment does not revoke the guardian's qualification, the people's court may, as needed, visit the minor and the minor's family, or may issue judicial suggestions to the local civil affairs department, the local police station, the village (neighborhood) committee, the Communist Youth League, the Women's Federation, the minor's school, the guardian's work unit, etc., to strengthen the protection of the minor and the supervision and guidance of the guardian.

38. The infringer whose guardian qualification has been revoked may, within a period from three months to one year after the date of revocation, apply in writing to the people's court for restoration of the guardian qualification, and shall submit relevant evidence.

The people's court shall notify the infringer and other guardians and designated guardians of the content of the preceding paragraph in writing.

39. The people's court shall try cases for restoration of guardian qualification in accordance with the case trial procedure for modification of guardianship relationships.

The people's court shall solicit the opinions of the minor's current guardian and the minor who has the ability to express opinions, and may entrust the minor rescue and protection institution of the applicant's place of residence or another minor protection organization to conduct an investigation into the applicant's guardianship willingness, repentance performance, guardianship ability, physical and mental condition, work and life situation, etc., and form an investigation and assessment report.

If the applicant is currently serving a criminal sentence or undergoing community correction, the people's court shall solicit the opinions of the penal enforcement authority or the community correctional institution.

40. Where, upon trial, the people's court finds that the applicant genuinely demonstrates repentance and is suitable to serve as a guardian, it may enter a judgment restoring the applicant's guardianship qualification, and the guardianship qualification of the originally appointed guardian shall terminate.

An applicant shall generally not be granted a judgment restoring guardianship qualification in any of the following circumstances:

(1) the applicant has committed sexual assault against a minor or sold a minor;

(2) the applicant has abused or abandoned a minor for a period of six months or more, or has abandoned a minor on multiple occasions, resulting in serious injury or more severe consequences; or

(3) the applicant has been sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of five years or more for a guardianship infringement act.

41. Within six months after the conclusion of the litigation for revocation of guardianship qualification, the minor and his or her current guardian may apply to the people's court for a personal safety protection order.

42. A parent whose guardianship qualification has been revoked shall continue to bear the child support expenses for the minor and all expenses arising from the guardianship infringement acts. Where relevant entities or individuals initiate an action in this regard, the people's court shall support it.

43. The civil affairs department shall, in accordance with relevant provisions, include minors who have suffered guardianship infringement and meet the conditions into the scope of social assistance and related security coverage.

44. Where the civil affairs department serves as the guardian, a child welfare institution undertaking the child-rearing duties may place the minor for adoption.

The placement of a minor for adoption shall be carried out no earlier than one year after the people's court renders the judgment revoking guardianship qualification. Where the infringer falls under the circumstances specified in paragraph 2 of Article 40 of this Opinion, the restriction of placement one year later shall not apply.
